newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Former Bangladesh president Ershad wins bail.
newsitem.headline: Former Bangladesh president Ershad wins bail.

text.p: Jailed former president Hossain Mohammad Ershad was granted bail by the Bangladesh Supreme Court on Wednesday in the last of a series of corruption charges, and was expected to be freed soon, court officials said.
Court sources told reporters Ershad was granted bail in a case involving corruption charges over the purchase of defence radar.
Officials said Ershad could be freed later on Wednesday or Thursday. He has been living in a special jail set up near the parliament house since winning a parliamentary seat in June elections.
His lawyers and leaders of his Jatiya Party were not immediately available.
Ershad, who seized power in a bloodless coup in 1982 and was deposed in an opposition-led people's uprising in 1990, at one time faced as many as 19 corruption charges.
He was sentenced to 23 years of imprisonment in four cases for keeping illegal firearms and corruption.
The High Court last year quashed his 10-year sentence for the arms offence, and Ershad has appealed against his other convictions.
Ershad won bail last November in what was the most sensational case against him -- the charge of killing Major-General Abul Manzur during a 1981 army mutiny.
Then-President General Ziaur Rahman, husband of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, was killed in the mutiny.
Ershad was then the army chief, and he later deposed Zia's vice-president and successor Justice Abdus Sattar in a bloodless coup in 1982.
Ershad's party lent support to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League to form the government following general election last June, which Khaleda's party lost.
